title: One-tape simulation with a space bound
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $f$ map words over $\Gamma$ to words over $\Gamma$, and let $T,S\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ in time $T$, and for every input $x$ and every time $t$ its space usage is at most $S(|x|)$. Then there are a finite alphabet $\Gamma'$ with decidable equality, an injection $e\colon\Gamma\hookrightarrow\Gamma'$, a finite Turing machine $M'$ over $\Gamma'$, and a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ such that $M'$ has one work tape, computes $f$ on symbolwise encoded inputs via $e$ within $c(T(n)+1)^2$ steps, and for every input $x$ and time $t$ uses at most $c(S(|x|)+1)$ work-tape cells.
hypotheses_covered: for all inputs $x$ and times $t$, space usage is at most $S(|x|)$
